newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean plantings 92 percent done - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean plantings 92 percent done - Safras.

text.p: Brazilian soybean plantings were 92 percent completed by December 12 against 84 percent by December 14, 1995 and an average of the past five years of 91 percent, consultants Safras e Mercado said.
Plantings by December 5 this year were 83 percent.

The return of rains in a large part of the producing areas helped replenish soil moisture levels in regions such as the south of Mato Grosso do Sul, the north and west of Parana, the west of Santa Catarina and the northwest of Rio Grande do Sul.
This means only some regions of Mato Grosso are currently waiting for general rains, Safras said in its weekly report.
In contrast with last year, planting should be virtually completed by the end of this week.
Last year a drought hit Rio Grande do Sul in particular, delaying plantings to the extent that 30 percent of sowings in the state were only done after Christmas.
Plantings of the 1996/97 crop by December 12 per state as estimated by Safras are as follows in percentage terms.

RIO GRANDE DO SUL - good advances. Main problem now is a lack of credit which should result in a smaller planted area than earlier anticipated. PARANA - climate helping plantings and confirming expectations of a record harvest above 6.5 million tonnes. MATO GROSSO - favorable conditions but throughout the state good rains are needed to finish off plantings. MATO GROSSO DO SUL - weather has returned to normal after a period of 10 days without rains. SAO PAULO - rains on December 11 and 12 arrived at just the right time and have helped keep conditions normal.
